title: Object/effects dispute — much logomachy from unequal definitions
source_text: XXXIV. Jam autem si quis quaerat quanti momenti sit illa quaestio de praedestinationis objecto atque effectibus, Respondeo in illa videri multum esse logomachiae. Etenim qui circa haec dissentiunt, praedestinationem non eodem modo definiunt: sed alii sub hac voce plura, alii vero pauciora decreta divina comprehendi volunt. Et hunc & illum actum divinae providentiae in praedestinatione includi hi quidem negant, illi vero affirmant. Nam qui praedestinationis objectum faciunt hominem creabilem vel possibilem, sic ampliant definitionem electionis & praedestinationis, ut illam ingrediatur divinum propositum de homine creando & lapsu ejus permittendo; imo nonnulli, ut Alphonsus Mendoza, universam providentiam ad praedestinationem quodammodo revocant. Quo posito necesse est effectum ejus esse creationem; & hominem consideratum, ut jam a Deo creandum, non recte ejus objectum constitui.
pass_a_gloss: But now if anyone ask of what moment that question is concerning the object and effects of predestination, I answer that in it there seems to be much logomachy. For those who dissent about these things do not define predestination in the same way: but some will have more divine decrees, others fewer, comprehended under this word. And that this or that act of divine providence is included in predestination these deny, those affirm. For those who make the object of predestination creatable or possible man so enlarge the definition of election and predestination that the divine purpose of creating man and of permitting his fall enters it; indeed some, as Alphonsus Mendoza, in a manner recall universal providence to predestination. Which being granted, it is necessary that its effect be creation; and man considered as already to be created by God is not rightly constituted its object.
pass_b_english: How much does the object/effects question matter? Much logomachy.
Dissenters define praedestinatio unequally — more vs fewer decrees under the word.
Creatable-object party enlarges the definition to include create-and-permit-fall.
Mendoza even draws universal providence toward praedestinatio — then creation must be an effect.
